audit_question.question: When takeSnapshot consumes a successful FileSnapshotSink.Close result, do the applicable sink and FSMSnapshot.Persist contracts ensure that the snapshot has completed the publication steps needed before snapshot metadata advances and logs are compacted, including legally reachable repeated-close and prior-error paths?
audit_question.importance: If orchestration treats an incomplete snapshot as published and then reclaims the corresponding logs, recovery evidence could become unavailable. The immediate question concerns the meaning of the consumed completion result; crash recovery failure and legal reachability of any problematic sequence remain separate questions.
event_paths: FSM snapshot capture -> FSMSnapshot.Persist -> sink Close -> last-snapshot update -> log compaction
counterevidence: The inventory describes fresh successful Close as completing finalization, metadata writing, rename, conditional directory synchronization and reaping; these are potential publication protections requiring exact-source review.
The inventory describes takeSnapshot as checking Persist and Close before updating metadata and compacting logs. Error propagation or contractual sink ownership may explain the entire concern.
unknowns: Exact contractual meaning of successful Close, including repeated calls.
Whether FSMSnapshot.Persist must close the sink and propagate every completion error.
Whether a contract-compliant execution can reach an already-closed sink after incomplete publication and subsequently return success to takeSnapshot.
Whether cancellation or other guards prevent consumption of an incomplete snapshot.
Which publication guarantees apply under noSync and operating-system variants.
Whether any locally distinguishable completion mismatch can lead to loss of recovery evidence in a legal history.
audit_question.trigger_rationale: The inventory explicitly limits F_file_snapshot_fresh_close to fresh calls, while its identified orchestration consumer relies on completion before reclaiming history. This is a concrete producer/consumer meaning gap to inspect, not evidence of a defect. No exact source is attached, so applicability and normative expectations remain unestablished.

selection_rationale: Select consumption of F_file_snapshot_fresh_close because the inventory identifies both a publication boundary and a downstream reclamation consumer, allowing a focused contract-and-code discriminator. Source review can either show that every contract-compliant successful consumption has the required publication meaning or identify a separately checkable local mismatch. Compared with F_reported_commit_threshold, this question requires fewer unresolved persistence producers and leader consumers. Compared with F_fsm_command_return, it offers an identified history-reclamation consequence without first resolving client-selected application semantics. These comparisons use inventory navigation only; no implementation conclusion or obligation is yet supported.
